title: Largest Local Values in a Matrix II
summary: Given an n x m matrix of non-negative integers, identify the non-zero cells that are local maxima.
statement: Given an n x m matrix of non-negative integers, identify the non-zero cells that are local maxima. A cell is considered a local maximum if it is non-zero and no cell within its x rows and x columns (excluding cells at the exact distance x) has a higher value. Count and return the number of such local maxima. For example, in the provided matrix, the cell at (3,3) with the value 2 is a local maximum because no other cell within its 2x2 area (excluding the corners) has a higher value.
constraints: matrix is nonempty, rectangular, and contains values from 0 through 200.
For a cell of value x, inspect the clipped square within x rows and columns, except positions whose row and column distances both equal x.
Only nonzero cells can be local maximums; equal values do not disqualify a cell.
hints: A candidate only needs to know whether its considered region contains a value greater than x.
Group candidates by value and build one two-dimensional prefix count of cells greater than that value.
Query the clipped square, then subtract the at most four excluded exact-distance corners when they are greater.
The remaining count is zero exactly for a local maximum; processing each distinct value bounds work by 200 matrix scans.
editorial: The remaining count is zero exactly for a local maximum; processing each distinct value bounds work by 200 matrix scans.

tests.explanation: The only nonzero cell has value two and no greater considered neighbor, so it is the sole local maximum.
Every smaller value considers a greater cell; only four remains a local maximum.
